*Longview Philanthropy is hiring a <https://www.longview.org/careers/chief-operating-officer/|COO / Director of Operations> to help us scale from 30 to 60 staff over the next 18 months.*

Longview is one of the world’s largest funders in AI safety and in nuclear security. We’re playing a lead role in some important areas like extreme AI-enabled power concentration, and we’re increasingly doing active grantmaking. We’re mission-driven, nimble, and scaling dramatically.

We’re looking for a senior operations leader to own our operations department (People Ops, BizOps, Finance, Talent, Grants Management) and build out new critical functions. You’ll work closely with our current COO, <https://www.longview.org/about/katie-hearsum/|Katie Hearsum>, who is transitioning to another senior role (e.g. Managing Director), and our CEO <https://www.longview.org/about/simran-dhaliwal/|Simran Dhaliwal>. 

The person we’re looking for:
• Has scaled an organization before from ~30 to ~60, ideally multiple times. 
• Is an experienced manager of managers 
• Has leadership experience in several ops functions
• Does not have to have AI safety or philanthropy background; we expect many of our strongest candidates will come from fast-scaling startups and tech companies.
:round_pushpin: SF, DC, NYC, or London (we can sponsor US and UK visas)
 :moneybag: $220K to 330K+ total comp for COO (or $165K to 264K+ for Director of Operations)
 :alarm_clock: Deadline: Sunday 6 September, <https://airtable.com/appOLeubwZNUCaamF/pagvzHRZzkbK2ndbF/form|application form here>

If you think <https://www.longview.org/careers/chief-operating-officer/|you’re an excellent fit> or know someone who might be, I encourage you to apply and/or pass along the posting!

*PauseAI UK is hiring: <https://pauseai.uk/jobs|pauseai.uk/jobs>*

Thousands of people across the UK believe that humanity might soon build dangerous superintelligent AI. And yet many of these people haven’t <https://pauseai.uk/campaigns|emailed their MP> about it. Political intervention is one of the most plausible ways that humanity can avoid catastrophe and there are many easy ways that anyone can help to improve the chance of useful AI legislation:
• You can just <https://pauseai.uk/campaigns|email your MP> and they may agree to <https://pauseai.info/dear-sir-demis-2025|sign a statement> supporting frontier AI legislation.
• You can just <https://pauseai.uk/track-record/#parliamentary-meetings|go to Parliament> and ask to meet with your MP and they might talk to you about AI for up to an hour.
• You can just march down the street in protest and newspapers <https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/ai-companies-public-relations-ae312d79?utm_source=luma|will> <https://www.businessinsider.com/protesters-accuse-google-deepmind-breaking-promises-ai-safety-2025-6?utm_source=luma|publish> <https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/03/02/1133814/i-checked-out-londons-biggest-ever-anti-ai-protest/?utm_source=luma|photos> <https://www.the-independent.com/tech/ai-safety-declaration-steve-bannon-b2932570.html?utm_source=luma|of> <https://gizmodo.com/the-openai-anthropic-cold-war-comes-to-illinois-2000746324?utm_source=luma|it> <https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/mar/06/uk-arts-must-not-be-sacrificed-for-speculative-ai-gains-peers-say?utm_source=luma|all> <https://youtu.be/-0CRojvk1FE?t=146&utm_source=luma|over> <https://www.wired.it/article/movimenti-contro-intelligenza-artificiale-mappa-nomi-pauseai-stopai-controlai/?utm_source=luma|the> <https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/rage-openai-protests?utm_source=luma|world>.
If the thousands of people that are already concerned about superintelligence were well organised as a political force, they could wield substantial power to influence British AI policy. Help us make that happen!

Reposting these policy opportunities (since I somehow missed that we have an opportunities channel):
> Federation of American Scientists has opened applications for its next AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship cohort.
> 
> If selected, you’ll work as a (paid) part-time FAS affiliate to advance your policy concept by engaging decision-makers, building coalitions, and pursuing opportunities for real-world policy impact. They’re looking for ideas across the frontier AI safety field, including:
> - Technical AI Safety: Ensuring frontier AI systems are reliable, aligned with human values, and behave predictably.
> - Governance and policy: Developing frameworks to guide the safe and secure use of frontier AI systems.
> - Risk assessment and mitigation for advanced AI systems.
> - Transparency and accountability: Enhancing these aspects in AI development and deployment.
> 
> You can apply at <https://fas.org/career/ai-safety-pef/>

> The <https://mail.horizonpublicservice.org/x/d?c=53000999&l=cd998ea8-bc51-4fe7-832b-b88072abde3e&r=fe66ad60-c763-4bf3-9eef-a0809ec38275|Horizon Fellowship> is accepting applications *until this Sunday, August 30 at 11:59pm Anywhere on Earth*. Please <https://mail.horizonpublicservice.org/x/d?c=53000999&l=8c96cebd-f3e3-4396-9f91-f8eb5cbd1f3b&r=fe66ad60-c763-4bf3-9eef-a0809ec38275|apply here> or share this opportunity with others in your network who may be interested in applying.
> 
> *About the fellowship:* 
> The Horizon Fellowship places fully-funded fellows in federal agencies, congressional offices, and top think tanks to help tackle policy challenges related to artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and other emerging technologies. Fellows selected for our program receive policy-focused training, mentorship, and support in matching with a host organization. For more information about the fellowship and eligibility, please visit <https://mail.horizonpublicservice.org/x/d?c=53000999&l=e8b5d7f7-f1b4-445f-9acd-fba6100c8abc&r=fe66ad60-c763-4bf3-9eef-a0809ec38275|this page>. 
> 
> *Program overview:*
> • Horizon fellows get 1-2 years of funding to work in full-time US policy roles at executive branch offices, Congressional offices, and think tanks in Washington, DC
> • Fellows are paid a salary of $78,000 - $190,000+ per year, depending on experience
> • Horizon has placed fellows at the Department of State, Commerce, and War; the White House; congressional committees; offices of individual senators and representatives; and prominent think tanks. You can learn more about past fellows and their placements at <https://mail.horizonpublicservice.org/x/d?c=53000999&l=f98014d2-5837-4679-b0b1-7e15ee664b65&r=fe66ad60-c763-4bf3-9eef-a0809ec38275|Meet our Fellows> and <https://mail.horizonpublicservice.org/x/d?c=53000999&l=ff638546-88c4-48cf-9366-77f5c50c2d47&r=fe66ad60-c763-4bf3-9eef-a0809ec38275|Fellow Accomplishments>
> • The program includes ten weeks of remote, part-time, work-compatible policy-focused training, mentorship, and access to an extended network of emerging tech policy professionals
> *Who is it for?*
> • Entry-level, mid-career, and senior candidates
> • Interested in realizing benefits and reducing risks from AI or biotech
> • Subject-matter expertise relevant to emerging tech (e.g. courses, work, research, or self-study)
> • Interested in public policy (though no prior policy experience required)
> • Willing to move to DC to start full-time work by Aug 2027
> • In most cases: Right to work in the US without employer sponsorship
> • Strong communication and writing skills
> • Able to build bridges with people with different perspectives
> • We strongly encourage folks from underrepresented groups to apply
> 
> 
> More information about the application process can be found in our <https://mail.horizonpublicservice.org/x/d?c=53000999&l=962968dd-efbd-4f3d-9498-9009bc8b7df8&r=fe66ad60-c763-4bf3-9eef-a0809ec38275|fellowship FAQ>. If you’d like to learn more about policy fellowships and how they can help you pivot into emerging technology policy, <https://mail.horizonpublicservice.org/x/d?c=53000999&l=d377e250-0998-4438-ac15-c9deccbc4f4f&r=fe66ad60-c763-4bf3-9eef-a0809ec38275|read our fellowship guide here>.
